document.title: Lazy CJK fallback via Droid Sans Fallback Full, with runtime fonts downloaded at configure time
document.summary: The glyph cache gains a third fallback font, Droid Sans Fallback Full, which the font registry opens on the first character the requested font and DejaVu Sans both lack. Both runtime fonts now leave git: one CMake function, shared with Twemoji, downloads them pinned by SHA-256 into the gitignored `assets/fonts`, and a build that cannot download them still boots with fallbacks.
document.why: Issue #50 asks for full Unicode text; the approved [revised proposal](source:s1) falls back from the requested font to DejaVu Sans to a bundled CJK font, with the CJK font loading on first miss. The [repo rule](source:s2) keeps font binaries out of git and has the build download them, with a fallback when that fails.

sources.title: Fonts: non-ASCII glyphs, size-independent atlases, package fonts on buttons
sources.gist: Revised proposal: dynamic glyph cache, DejaVu Sans then Droid Sans Fallback Full as fallbacks, Twemoji colour emoji; three PRs.

sources.label: Máté's rule after reviewing #91
sources.gist: No font or emoji binaries in git; the build system downloads all fonts into a gitignored folder, with a fallback when the download fails.

lookFor: Droid Sans Fallback Full has no Hangul syllables, so Korean still draws DejaVu's missing-glyph box; the [proposal](source:s1) does not mention this, and the smoke line uses `日本語 かな 中文` instead of Korean.
The downloaded `DejaVuSans.ttf` is the upstream 2.37 release build (757,076 bytes), not the 759,720-byte 2.37 build that was vendored; the smoke golden still matches within tolerance.

The Droid font comes from GitHub's `aosp-mirror/platform_frameworks_base` at the `android-7.1.2_r39` commit, because android.googlesource.com serves raw files only as base64; the bytes match the previously vendored file.

groups.title: Three-font fallback chain in the glyph cache
groups.why: The [proposal](source:s1) puts a CJK font after DejaVu Sans and loads it on first miss.
groups.summary: `glyph_cache_get` walks the requested font, the fallback, then the font `glyph_cache_set_fallback_loader`'s callback opens once; `has_glyph` asks the same three fonts for an emoji's first character, and the harness skips the cases that need a downloaded font when it is missing.
lookFor: Subtle: any codepoint both earlier fonts lack opens the 4 MB font, not only CJK; a private-use character such as U+E000 in a Latin-only app triggers the load once.
A loader that returns NULL is consumed anyway, so a missing font file logs one warning and later misses go straight to the missing-glyph box.
Subtle: an emoji without an image whose first character only the CJK font has, like `日` + U+FE0F, now opens the 4 MB font through `has_glyph` instead of drawing U+FFFD.

groups.title: Configure-time download of runtime fonts and Twemoji
groups.why: The [repo rule](source:s2) keeps font and emoji binaries out of git; the build downloads them and falls back when it cannot.
groups.summary: `vitadeck_fetch_asset` in `cmake/fetch_asset.cmake` downloads, hash-checks and stamps each pin; `cmake/twemoji.cmake` and `cmake/fonts.cmake` call it, and `CMakeLists.txt` packs only the fonts that arrived into the VPK and `upload_vita`.
lookFor: A failed download only warns at configure time, so CI goes green without fonts; the smoke golden is what catches a missing DejaVu Sans or Droid font.
Stamps live in `assets/.downloads`, not in `assets/emoji`, because `FILE assets/emoji` ships that folder whole in the VPK.
A stamp whose listed files are gone triggers a fresh download, so deleting `assets/fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf` by hand heals on the next configure.

groups.title: Font registry owns the Runtime Fallback Font
groups.why: The chain needs a loader that owns the font, and the device needs the file in the VPK.
groups.summary: `load_fallback_font` in `fonts.c` opens `assets/fonts/DroidSansFallbackFull.ttf` for the glyph cache and frees it at shutdown; the licence file stays tracked and names the download source.

groups.title: Raylib font when DejaVu Sans is missing
groups.why: The [repo rule](source:s2) needs a fallback when the download fails; without one `font_registry_init` failed and the app did not open.
groups.summary: `font_registry_init` becomes `void`: it logs one warning and gives the Runtime Default Font raylib's built-in font when `DejaVuSans.ttf` does not load, and `bootstrap.c` stops treating that as fatal.
lookFor: Raylib's built-in font has no ő, ű, CJK or emoji, so an offline build draws `?` for them; Deck App Fonts still fall back to the Droid font, if it downloaded.

groups.title: Smoke golden draws CJK
groups.why: The golden proves the fallback renders real glyphs on Linux.
groups.summary: The smoke header gets a `日本語 かな 中文` line beside the Hungarian text, and the Linux golden is refreshed to match.

groups.title: Glossary and SDK README
groups.why: The [proposal](source:s1) adds the Runtime Fallback Font term to CONTEXT.md.
groups.summary: `CONTEXT.md` adds **Runtime Fallback Font** and the raylib fallback of the Runtime Default Font in place, the SDK README names the CJK coverage, and `AGENTS.md` and the build skill say configure downloads the fonts.

commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
origin/main's tree matches #91's head 8468e93, which this branch already
contains, so every file keeps the branch side. Git's auto-merge had
duplicated the SDK README emoji paragraph; that is dropped too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: build: keep download stamps out of the shipped asset folders
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The Twemoji stamp lists 4,009 file names, and assets/emoji ships whole
in the VPK. Stamps and staging now live in the gitignored
assets/.downloads, which CI caches with the assets.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Without assets/fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf or DroidSansFallbackFull.ttf the
harness says which cases it skips and runs the rest on the ASCII
fixture. A new case checks that an emoji without an image takes its
first character from the Runtime Fallback Font.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(ui): draw with raylib's font when DejaVu Sans did not download
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A build without the Runtime Default Font now boots with one warning and
draws that font with raylib's built-in font, so the Shell and the Deck
App Failure Screen still work. Emoji base-character fallback asks the
Runtime Fallback Font too, like the glyph chain.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: build: download DejaVu Sans at configure time
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The Runtime Default Font leaves git too: cmake/fonts.cmake extracts
DejaVuSans.ttf from the pinned DejaVu 2.37 dejavu-sans-ttf release zip
into assets/fonts, so src/ui/fonts.c keeps its path. This is the
upstream release build; the file it replaces was a different 2.37 build.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: build: download Droid Sans Fallback Full at configure time
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The Runtime Fallback Font leaves git: cmake/fonts.cmake fetches it from
AOSP's android-7.1.2_r39 tag on the GitHub mirror, pinned by commit and
SHA-256, into the gitignored assets/fonts. The VPK and upload_vita only
ship the runtime fonts that downloaded; CI caches assets/fonts beside
assets/emoji.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: build: one pinned-download function for configure-time assets
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
cmake/fetch_asset.cmake holds the download, SHA-256 check, stamp and
warning-only failure that cmake/twemoji.cmake had inline; Twemoji now
calls it with the same pin and folder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
An emoji cluster whose Twemoji image is missing, as when the download
failed, now draws once as a whole: its first codepoint from the font or
the Runtime Default Font, else U+FFFD, instead of a .notdef box per
codepoint. Misses stay cached, so no image is looked up twice.

commits.subject: build: download Twemoji at configure time instead of vendoring it
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
cmake/twemoji.cmake fetches the pinned v17.0.3 tag archive once, checks
its SHA-256, extracts only assets/72x72 into the gitignored assets/emoji
and drops -fe0f from the names. A failed download warns and the build
carries on without images. CI caches the folder.

commits.subject: feat(ui): colour emoji in the glyph atlas
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Emoji clusters (single, U+FE0F, skin tones, flags, keycaps, ZWJ) resolve
to the longest Twemoji sequence with an image, resampled to the Font Size

commits.subject: feat: Button font and fontSize props
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The native Button takes a font name after the label; an unset fontSize passes 0 and the host default of 20 applies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(ui): draw text through the glyph cache with Runtime Default Font fallback
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
TrueType and OpenType fonts load as font bytes instead of a pre-baked 64 px atlas, so startup does no rasterising. Text, Button and TextInput measure and draw through text.c; each frame caches the glyphs it draws, then uploads changed atlas pages once before drawing, because vitaGL copies a whole texture that changes after it was drawn. .fnt and .bdf fonts keep raylib's path. Word-wrap chunking no longer splits a UTF-8 sequence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(ui): on-demand glyph cache over stb_truetype
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Glyphs rasterise at the exact pixel size on first use, keyed by (font, size, codepoint), into 1024x1024 RGBA8 atlas pages (4 MiB, at most 4). When every page is full, the least recently used one not used this frame is cleared. A codepoint the font lacks comes from the fallback font, else the font's .notdef.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: chore(vendor): stb_truetype v1.26, the copy raylib 5.5 compiles
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
raylib builds its copy with STBTT_STATIC and installs no external headers, so the glyph cache needs its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
